physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the sacral plexus, the knot of nerves at the floor of the spine, low in the belly, where the body keeps its readiness to move. It is the place a person feels life force before they have a word for it, the warmth in the pelvis when something genuinely interests them, the dull weight there when nothing does. This is the code of small persistent motion, and the sacral is where the body decides, beneath thinking, whether to go.

The shadow has its bodily floor here. When the days run in a circle, the sacral does not go quiet so much as scatter, a jittered hum that drives the limbs through chores without ever choosing a direction. The legs walk and walk and the body arrives back where it started. Other times it dims to a flat heaviness in the lower belly, no pull toward anything, the engine on but disengaged.

The climb out is also bodily, and it is small. A first step taken before the mind has agreed to it. A pull from low in the pelvis, the kind a child follows without asking why. Determination, in the body, is not a clench of the jaw. It is the sacral finding one direction and giving its small steady yes to it, again, until the legs are moving along a true line and the rest is following.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the organ, this code answers to a single amino acid, Threonine. Threonine belongs to the small group the body cannot make for itself. It comes in through the mouth and must be carried in from the world before any of its work can begin.

What it does in the body is quiet and fitting. Threonine helps build the connective tissue, the tendons and the small bands that hold a joint together and let it move without coming apart. It is a chemistry of articulation, of one small piece linking truly to the next. The body of a person who walks is held together by this.

The card has been saying the same thing in every voice. One step, then another, in the same direction, until a path takes shape. The chemistry says it lower down. The code that teaches you to move forward through small linked acts runs on the molecule that links the body's small parts into something that can carry you.
